status.description: Status of the invocation

status_reason.description: A nonempty, customer-safe summary of the recorded failure output, always present when status is failed and omitted otherwise. Recognized messages receive a specific summary; other failures receive a generic summary. Message matching does not establish whether the failure originated in the platform or action code. Does not include raw action output or internal error details. Human-readable text, not a stable identifier for retry logic.

country.description: ISO 3166 country code. Supported countries are US, GB, FR, DE, SG, and KR. Defaults to US if not provided, or to the country of ip_address when that is set.

ip_address.description: Reserved exit IP to pin the proxy to. Available only to organizations with a reserved ISP allocation; the IP must be active in it (see GET /proxy_ips) and, when country is also set, in that country. Omit to let Kernel choose an IP. A proxy read includes it only when the proxy's primary exit IP is one of the organization's reserved IPs; every ISP proxy's exit IP is on the top-level ip_address. An IP outside the allocation is rejected with code ip_not_reserved; one that cannot currently be assigned, with 409 ip_unavailable.

IspProxyUpdateConfig.description: Changes to an ISP proxy's exit IP. Accepted only for proxies of type `isp`.

ip_address.description: Reserved exit IP to move the proxy to. The IP must be active in the organization's allocation and in the proxy's country. The proxy keeps its ID. The new endpoint is probed before anything changes; a failed probe leaves the proxy as it was. Live browsers open new connections on the new IP within a few seconds; established connections drain on the old one.

KernelCardState.description: A ready Kernel card funded by a payment method supports authorize, fill, then submit checkout. A single-use card (source single_use_card) is ready on creation, supports only fill, and is expired from expires_at; Kernel deletes its stored details shortly after expires_at. It has no payment_method_id or funding_status. Card details are delivered for a few minutes after fill; submit promptly. Repeated fill is safe and never submits checkout. Visa purchases require a spend_approval action before details are issued; Mastercard purchases need no hosted approval. masks.last4 is the enrolled card's last four digits; masks.token_last4, when present, is the token's last four digits shown to the merchant. Kernel does not observe whether the merchant charged the card.

domains.description: Informational registrable domain. Fill is locked to merchant_url's exact origin, except that a single-use card fills on any https page of this registrable domain.

funding_status.description: Whether payment_method_id can still fund this purchase. unavailable means the method is being removed or awaits recovery, so authorization, fill and confirmation are refused until it recovers. removed means the method was removed from its wallet, so this purchase can no longer be paid; create a new purchase with another method. Neither changes status, which still reports what already happened to this purchase.

payment_method_id.description: Wallet-scoped ID of the payment method funding this purchase. It is bound when the purchase is created and never changes; purchases created before payment methods could be selected report the wallet's default card, card.

source.description: payment_method for a purchase funded by a wallet payment method; single_use_card for a card whose details were supplied with single_use_card.

status.description: pending_authorization waits for cardholder approval on Visa purchases or fresh security-code collection on alias-mode purchases through the spend_approval action; an unused link expires after 30 minutes. Alias-mode cards become ready after collection and expire at the temporary security-code alias deadline, by default five minutes later. An expired alias purchase requires a new card. recovery_required means verification, approving the purchase or issuing the one-time code has an unresolved outcome. A server-classified initial attestation failure before intent dispatch may advertise restart_verification to prepare a fresh local verification link; this does not approve spending or replay any provider request. Unclassified legacy recovery and uncertain intent creation cannot restart. Kernel never approves again or issues another code for the item automatically. To continue, delete this card and create a new purchase; the cardholder approves the new purchase separately. Recovery while reporting a merchant transaction cannot be deleted and must be reconciled with support. When status_reason says the provider refused retrieval before acceptance, no code was issued and a later read retries. declined means the card network refused to issue a code.

KernelCardVaultItemSpec.description: One live purchase with a Kernel-enrolled card. Authorization obtains an agentic network token number, expiry and one-time 3-digit code. They are stored encrypted for the fill operation, which types them only on merchant_url's origin; the merchant's own checkout submits the payment. The one-time code is valid until the item's expires_at; fill and submit checkout before then. Mastercard purchases need no cardholder approval. A Visa purchase returns a spend_approval action: the cardholder approves it with a Visa passkey, and Kernel registers a Visa intent for one transaction up to the amount before issuing the code. For supported cards whose network cannot be enrolled for agentic tokens, authorize returns pending_authorization with a spend_approval action to collect a fresh security code in a hosted field. Once collected, the card is ready and can be filled before its expires_at, by default five minutes after collection. An expired card requires a new purchase. Fill types those details on merchant_url's origin. The amount, merchant_url and merchant_country are recorded but do not restrict payment requests sent by the browser. Card updates are not supported; delete and create a new item instead. With single_use_card the item is instead a single-use card whose details the caller supplies, such as a virtual card from its issuer. It is not funded by a payment method, is ready on creation, and supports only fill: Kernel stores the details encrypted, never returns them, and fills them on any https page whose registrable domain (state.domains) is merchant_url's, including its subdomains. Fill does not consume it. From expires_at it is expired and can no longer be filled; Kernel deletes its stored details shortly after expires_at. Deleting the card, its wallet or its vault deletes them immediately. amount, currency and the merchant fields are recorded but not enforced. Repeating the identical request returns the existing card; any other request with the same key returns 409, as does repeating it once the expired card's details have been deleted.

amount.description: Integer amount in minor currency units (at most 1000000), bound to the one-time code.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Supported: aud, brl, cad, chf, czk, dkk, eur, gbp, hkd, inr, jpy, krw, mxn, nok, nzd, pln, sek, sgd, usd, zar.

expires_at.description: Single-use cards only. From this time the card is expired and can no longer be filled; Kernel deletes its stored details shortly after. Deleting the card, its wallet or its vault deletes them immediately. Defaults to 2 hours after creation, capped at the end of the card's expiry month; a requested time must be in the future, at most 24 hours after creation, and not after the end of the card's expiry month. Returned in UTC.

merchant_category.description: Actual merchant category when known. Omit rather than invent a category.

merchant_category_code.description: Actual merchant MCC when known. Omit rather than invent a code. 0000 is not accepted.

merchant_country.description: The merchant's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required for Visa cards, whose one-time code is issued for the merchant's country.

merchant_url.description: Merchant checkout URL. Fill is allowed only on this URL's origin.

payment_method_id.description: Wallet-scoped payment method ID from the wallet's payment_methods expansion. Omission selects the wallet's default card, ID card, for compatibility with existing requests; it never falls back to another method, and a wallet without a default card requires the ID. The purchase is bound to the method's enrolled card and network token, so later operations cannot switch funding. Not allowed with single_use_card.

wallet.description: Key of the Kernel wallet item whose enrolled card pays.

description.description: Recognizable site or service name displayed verbatim as the form title, without suffixes such as sign-in credentials. Display text only, not an enforced destination policy.

fields.description: Ordered field definitions rendered in this order by credential collection forms.

KernelCredentialVaultItemSpecInput.description: Credential fields are for login and other non-payment credentials. Do not store, collect, or fill credit card data in credential items. Use wallet, payment_request and card item types for credit cards and payment checkout instead. Field order is preserved in the user-facing collection form, so list fields in the same top-to-bottom order as the website.

description.description: The site's recognizable display name, used verbatim as the user-facing form title (for example, Hacker News). Use only the site or service name; do not append sign-in, login, credentials, or task instructions. This is display text, not an enforced destination policy. At most 16 KiB in UTF-8 bytes.

fields.description: Ordered field definitions. Use the website's top-to-bottom field order; the collection form renders this order unchanged.
Exactly one entry for each declared field.

status.description: Ready means all required fields have values, not that a login succeeded. Optional fields may remain unset.

KernelManagedLinkAuthorizationInput.description: Kernel starts and completes the user's Link authorization flow.

KernelPaymentRequestVaultItemSpec.description: One live purchase funded by the Kernel wallet payment method named by payment_method_id. The method must be active and eligible when the request is created. The purchase is bound to that method; later operations cannot switch funding, and removing the method makes the purchase unusable rather than moving it to another card. Approval, issuance, fill and the alias fallback behave as described for KernelCardVaultItemSpec.

amount.description: Integer amount in minor currency units (at most 1000000), bound to the one-time code.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Supported: aud, brl, cad, chf, czk, dkk, eur, gbp, hkd, inr, jpy, krw, mxn, nok, nzd, pln, sek, sgd, usd, zar.

merchant_category.description: Actual merchant category when known. Omit rather than invent a category.

merchant_category_code.description: Actual merchant MCC when known. Omit rather than invent a code. 0000 is not accepted.

merchant_country.description: The merchant's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required for Visa cards, whose one-time code is issued for the merchant's country.

merchant_url.description: Merchant checkout URL. Fill is allowed only on this URL's origin.

payment_method_id.description: Payment method ID from the wallet's payment_methods expansion.

wallet.description: Key of the Kernel wallet item that owns the payment method.

KernelSingleUseCard.description: Details of a card the caller supplies, such as a single-use virtual card from its issuer. Mutually exclusive with payment_method_id. The card details are stored encrypted for fill and never returned; reads return only reference. Kernel deletes them shortly after the card's expires_at; deleting the card, its wallet or its vault deletes them immediately. A card whose expiry month has ended is rejected.

name.description: Cardholder name, filled as billing_name.

number.description: Card number; must pass the Luhn check.

reference.description: The caller's identifier for the card, such as the issuer's card ID. Returned unchanged on reads.

status.description: connected means the wallet is usable. It holds zero or more cards as payment methods, listed by the payment_methods expansion, and each can pay once it reports capabilities.single_use_card.eligible. A wallet with no cards, before its first card or after its last is removed, is still connected. Where the wallet advertises add_payment_method and remove_payment_method, use them to manage cards. Otherwise the wallet enrolls one default card when created; until that card is enrolled the wallet reports pending_authorization with the card's card_enrollment action, or degraded when the card's enrollment outcome is unknown and the wallet must be deleted before adding another card. reconnect_required appears only on a wallet created before cards were payment methods and not yet upgraded. Reads preserve its stored state until the operator upgrade; payment and deletion requests are refused until then.

KernelWalletVaultItemSpec.description: Cards stored with Kernel-managed credentials, each a payment method of the wallet. Each card is enrolled through a card_enrollment action: the cardholder enters the card and their email on a Kernel-hosted page. Where the wallet advertises add_payment_method, creation returns an empty connected wallet and each card is enrolled with that operation. Otherwise creation returns the wallet's default card's card_enrollment action, and the wallet connects once that card is stored. Kernel then enrolls each card for an agentic network token when the issuer supports it. The card number never reaches Kernel. The connected wallet's payment_methods expansion lists the cards; capabilities.single_use_card.eligible is false, with a network_token_* reason, until the card has a network token, and authorize returns 400 for such a card unless Kernel supports checkout delivery without a network token for that card. In that case, fill types the checkout details. Visa purchases require the cardholder to complete a spend_approval action before Kernel issues a one-time code; Mastercard purchases need no hosted approval.

LinkAgentWalletSpendLimits.description: Link's agent wallet spend limits, per transaction and over rolling periods.

LinkAgentWalletStepUp.description: Verification Link requires from the user before the agent wallet can spend.

action_url.description: URL where the user completes verification; null when no action is available.

status.description: Link status such as not_required, ssn_verification, identity_verification, contact_support or complete.

LinkCardState.description: Issued Link cards retain encrypted card material for the fill operation. Link cards do not expose aliases or support egress substitution.

credential_type.description: The Link spend request's credential_type, set when authorize sends the request to Link. Absent before authorize and after Link rejects the request; a ready card without it fills like card. card is a Link virtual card; fill it with field bindings. link_pay_token is a Link Pay Token that Kernel supplies through the checkout's Link WebMCP tool; fill it without fields.

status.description: recovery_required means an original provider operation has an unresolved outcome and the card cannot be used. Reads keep observing a known provider request and may clear the recovery. To continue, delete this card and create a new one; deleting cancels the original request when its ID is known and keeps the recovery evidence. The user may see an approval request for the original card and should approve only the new one.

LinkCardVaultItemSpec.description: Live Link card request. Test-mode card creation is not supported. The spec can be changed with PATCH until the card is authorized at a checkout. Authorize it with the browser at final checkout: Kernel inspects the checkout through WebMCP and internally chooses a merchant-bound Link Pay Token when supported or a virtual card otherwise. Callers do not choose how the credential is delivered; after authorize, state.credential_type reports it.

amount.description: Integer amount in minor currency units, at most 50000. With recurring, the spending limit per period, not a lifetime total.

payment_method_id.description: Payment-method ID returned by the referenced wallet's payment-method listing. The provider decides whether the selected funding method can satisfy the card request.

unit_amount.description: Unit amount in minor currency units.

LinkRecurring.description: Recurring terms for a subscription or other repeated purchase. The amount becomes the spending limit for each period of interval_count intervals, for example every 2 weeks. The merchant schedules charges. The card stays ready after each charge until it expires or is deleted; do not create a new card each period. Deleting the card, its wallet or its vault first cancels the credential with Link, so later charges decline; if Link cannot be reached, deletion returns 409 provider_revocation_pending and should be retried. Deletion does not cancel the subscription with the merchant. Recurring terms cannot be changed once the card is authorized.

interval_count.description: Number of intervals per period. Link defaults it to 1.

limit.description: Null means unlimited.

remaining.description: Amount still available in the rolling period; null means unlimited.

used.description: Amount already spent in the rolling period.

LinkShippingAddress.description: One entry of Link's `GET /shipping_addresses` response, passed through as Link reports it. Kernel never stores it.

LinkShippingAddressDetails.description: Link's nullable postal address fields. Omitted from the shipping address when Link reports null.

limit.description: Null means unlimited.

LinkTokenRefresh.description: Who refreshes an imported Link grant. kernel (default) means Kernel holds and rotates the refresh token. customer means your backend keeps the refresh token and replaces the access token with update_access_token; Kernel never refreshes or revokes the grant. Fixed at wallet creation.

amount.description: Total amount in minor currency units.

LinkUserInfo.description: Link's `GET /userinfo` response for the connected wallet, passed through as Link reports it when the `link_user_info` expansion is requested. Kernel never stores it. Null fields are null at Link; omitted fields were not reported. Amounts are in the minor unit of `default_spend_request_currency`.

default_spend_request_currency.description: Lowercase ISO currency Link applies to a spend request created without one.

eligible_for_balance.description: Whether the user can fund purchases from a Link balance.

LinkUserInfoAddress.description: The Link user's postal address. Omitted when Link reports none.

LinkWalletTokenInput.description: Send the tokens from your backend. Supply a currently valid access token. With token_refresh=kernel, also send the refresh token from the same Link grant under the referenced client; Kernel refreshes when needed after import and uses the expiry returned by Link for subsequent tokens. With token_refresh=customer, omit the refresh token. Tokens are never returned in wallet responses, events, or logs.

refresh_token.description: Required with token_refresh=kernel; rejected with token_refresh=customer.

ListFiles.description: Array of file or directory information entries.

LoginResponse.description: Response from starting a login flow

hosted_url.description: URL to redirect user to for login

live_view_url.description: Browser live view URL for watching the login flow

MFAOption.description: An MFA method option for verification

MFAType.description: The MFA delivery method type. Includes 'password' for auth method selection pages and 'switch' for generic method-switcher links like "Use another method" that do not name a specific method.

ManagedAuth.description: Managed authentication that keeps a profile logged into a specific domain. Flow fields (flow_status, flow_step, discovered_fields, mfa_options) reflect the most recent login flow and are null when no flow has been initiated.

allowed_domains.description: Additional hostname roots valid for this auth flow, besides the primary domain. Each value allows credential entry on that exact hostname and its subdomains. Leading `www.` and `*.` labels are normalized away. When omitted or empty, credential entry is unrestricted. The following SSO/OAuth provider domains are automatically allowed by default and do not need to be specified: - Google: accounts.google.com - Microsoft/Azure AD: login.microsoftonline.com, login.live.com - Okta: *.okta.com, *.oktapreview.com - Auth0: *.auth0.com, *.us.auth0.com, *.eu.auth0.com, *.au.auth0.com - Apple: appleid.apple.com - GitHub: github.com - Facebook/Meta: www.facebook.com - LinkedIn: www.linkedin.com - Amazon Cognito: *.amazoncognito.com - OneLogin: *.onelogin.com - Ping Identity: *.pingone.com, *.pingidentity.com

auto_reauth.description: Whether automatic re-authentication is permitted for this connection. This is an opt-in flag only — it does not check whether re-auth is actually feasible. Even when true, re-auth only runs when the system has what it needs to perform it (for example, saved credentials for the required login fields), and only after a scheduled health check detects an expired session — so this flag has no effect when `health_checks` is false. When false, expired sessions detected by a health check are marked as `NEEDS_AUTH` instead of attempting re-auth.

browser.description: Default browser configuration for login, reauthentication, and health-check sessions.

browser_session_id.description: ID of the underlying browser session driving the current flow (present when flow in progress). Use this to inspect or terminate the browser session via the `/browsers` API.

browser_telemetry.description: Deprecated. Use browser.telemetry. Retained during migration for existing clients.

can_reauth.description: Whether this connection's stored requirements are eligible for unattended re-authentication. A true value can represent either fully satisfiable requirements or a best-effort attempt. It does not account for whether automatic re-authentication is enabled or parent workflow state such as an active flow or circuit-breaker cooldown, so it does not guarantee an attempt on the next health check. See `can_reauth_reason` for the specific outcome.

can_reauth_reason.description: Machine-readable reason for the current value of `can_reauth`. Affirmative values (requirements are eligible for unattended re-authentication): - `external_credential` — an external credential provider is attached - `cua_has_credential` — CUA flow with a stored credential - `has_credential` — Kernel credential is attached (optimistic; plan viability not checked) - `viable_plans_found` — at least one stored login plan can be replayed - `no_requirements_recorded` — no recorded credential requirements to fail against - `totp_reauth_allowed` — TOTP is the only recorded requirement and a stored secret can generate the code - `optimistic_totp_attempt` — TOTP was previously required but no reusable secret is stored; the connection remains eligible for a circuit-breaker-bounded attempt because the site may not challenge returning sessions - `requirements_satisfiable` — recorded requirements contain no recognized blocker Negative values (a human must complete the login flow): - `no_prior_successful_login` — connection has never completed a successful login - `no_credential` — no Kernel or external credential attached - `no_viable_plans` — credential attached but no replayable login plan exists yet - `viable_plans_require_external_action` — stored plans need an external step (email link, push, etc.) - `requires_external_action` — recorded requirements include an external step - `requires_totp_without_secret` — flow needs a TOTP code but no TOTP secret is stored - `requires_sms_code` — flow needs an SMS code that cannot be received automatically - `requires_email_code` — flow needs an email code that cannot be received automatically - `requires_customer_input` — flow needs another field or choice that is unavailable during unattended re-authentication

choices.description: Canonical choices awaiting selection. Prefer this over pending_sso_buttons, mfa_options, and sign_in_options when present.

discovered_fields.description: Fields awaiting input (present when flow_step=awaiting_input; may also be present with awaiting_external_action as fallback actions)

external_action_message.description: Instructions for external action (present when flow_step=awaiting_external_action)

fields.description: Canonical fields awaiting input. Prefer this over discovered_fields when present.

flow_expires_at.description: When the current flow expires (null when no flow in progress). A flow past this timestamp is no longer valid and its `flow_status` will be `EXPIRED`. Clients may start a new login to supersede a stale `IN_PROGRESS` flow past this timestamp.

flow_status.description: Current flow status (null when no flow in progress)

flow_step.description: Current step in the flow (null when no flow in progress)

flow_type.description: Type of the current flow (null when no flow in progress)

health_check_interval.description: Interval in seconds between automatic health checks. When set, the system periodically verifies the authentication status and triggers re-authentication if needed. Maximum is 86400 (24 hours). Default is 3600 (1 hour) or your plan minimum, whichever is larger. The minimum depends on your plan: Enterprise: 300 (5 minutes), Startup: 1200 (20 minutes), Hobbyist: 3600 (1 hour), Free: 21600 (6 hours).

health_check_unavailable_reason.description: Why health checks cannot verify this connection. Present when health checks are enabled but no auth check URL is available; a recent last_auth_check_at is not evidence of a valid session.

health_checks.description: Whether periodic health checks are enabled for this connection. When false, the system will not automatically verify authentication status, and `auto_reauth` has no effect on the automatic flow (since re-auth is only triggered by a failed scheduled health check). Manually triggering a health check via the API still works regardless of this setting.

hitl.description: Whether a login blocked by a CAPTCHA the browser cannot solve pauses at AWAITING_HUMAN_INTERVENTION so a person can complete it in the live view.

hosted_url.description: URL to redirect user to for hosted login (present when flow in progress)

id.description: Unique identifier for the auth connection

interaction_id.description: Opaque identifier for the current canonical interaction. Required when submitting fields or choices and changes for each new actionable pause.

last_auth_at.description: Deprecated alias for `last_auth_check_at`. Despite the name, this is the last health-check timestamp, not the last successful authentication. Use `last_auth_check_at` instead.

last_auth_check_at.description: When the most recent auth health check ran for this connection, regardless of outcome. Updated on every health check and does not by itself indicate that the profile is currently authenticated - use `status` for that. May be newer than `flow_expires_at` when a flow is still in progress because health checks continue to run in parallel.

live_view_url.description: Browser live view URL for debugging (present when flow in progress)

login_url.description: Optional login page URL to skip discovery

mfa_options.description: MFA method options (present when flow_step=awaiting_input; may also be present with awaiting_external_action as fallback actions)

pending_sso_buttons.description: SSO buttons available (present when flow_step=awaiting_input; may also be present with awaiting_external_action as fallback actions)

post_login_url.description: URL where the browser landed after successful login

profile_name.description: Name of the profile associated with this auth connection

proxy_id.description: Deprecated. Read browser.proxy instead. Retained during migration for existing clients.

record_session.description: Whether to record browser session replays for this connection by default. Useful for debugging login flows. Can be overridden per-login.

save_credentials.description: Whether credentials are saved after every successful login. One-time codes (TOTP, SMS, etc.) are not saved.

sign_in_options.description: Non-MFA choices presented during the auth flow, such as account selection or org pickers (present when flow_step=awaiting_input; may also be present with awaiting_external_action as fallback actions).

sso_provider.description: SSO provider being used (e.g., google, github, microsoft)

status.description: Last known authentication status of the managed profile. An inconclusive health check preserves this status and does not verify the current session.

website_error.description: Visible error message from the website (e.g., 'Incorrect password'). Present when the website displays an error during login.

ManagedAuthBrowserConfig.description: Browser configuration applied to browser sessions created for a managed auth connection. Managed auth controls the profile, headless mode, timeout, start URL, kiosk mode, and viewport.

captcha_solver.description: Automatic CAPTCHA solving for managed auth browser sessions. When provided without stealth, stealth no longer defaults to true. Enabling it does not select a proxy: a connection on direct egress stays there; set proxy.mode=default for Kernel's default stealth proxy. Turning it off on a connection that uses Kernel's default stealth proxy moves it to direct egress. Omit on update to keep the current setting, or on login to inherit it.

location.description: Browser locale for the connection's login, reauthentication, and health-check sessions. Set on create or update; not supported on login.

proxy.description: Proxy configuration for managed auth browser sessions. Omit on create to derive the default from stealth, or on update and login to preserve or inherit the connection default.

region.description: Browser region. Omit on create to use us-east, on update to keep the current region, or on login to inherit it. Login overrides apply only to that login. Non-default regions require an eligible plan and organization access.

stealth.description: Whether managed auth browser sessions use stealth mode: CAPTCHA solving with Kernel's default stealth proxy unless proxy is set. Defaults to true when neither stealth nor captcha_solver is provided. Cannot be combined with captcha_solver.enabled=false. Setting it does not change an existing proxy, including direct egress; use proxy.mode=default for Kernel's default stealth proxy. Reports true for a connection with only captcha_solver enabled; proxy shows its egress. Deprecated in favor of captcha_solver and proxy.

telemetry.description: Browser telemetry configuration using the same semantics as browser create.

ManagedAuthBrowserLocation.description: Browser locale applied to browser sessions created for a managed auth connection.

locale.description: Supported canonical BCP 47 locale for the browser's language and Accept-Language header. Omit to use the default for the browser's region, or omit on update to keep the current locale. Null clears it on update.

ManagedAuthChoice.description: Canonical auth-flow choice awaiting user selection.

display_text.description: Display text captured for a choice.

id.description: Stable choice identifier for canonical submit.

ManagedAuthCredentialVaultItemSpecInput.description: A credential backed by a managed auth connection. The item stores no values: it reads the connection's saved credential at fill time, so updates made through managed auth apply immediately. The connection must be in the vault's project and hold a saved Kernel credential. The check is the saved credential, not connection status: a connection that needs re-authentication qualifies, and an authenticated one without a saved credential does not. Returns 404 for an unknown connection, and 409 when the connection is in another project, has no saved credential yet, or uses an external credential provider such as 1Password. No collection form is offered; managed auth collects the login.

connection_id.description: ID of the managed auth connection whose saved credential this item reads. List connections with `GET /auth/connections`.

description.description: Optional display text for the item, such as the site or service name. Set at creation and cannot be changed later; repeating the request with a different description returns 409. At most 16 KiB in UTF-8 bytes.

fields.description: One entry per non-empty value on the connection's saved credential, keyed by the field name to use in fill bindings. Included on single-item responses (create and get) and omitted from list responses, like `value_keys` on credentials. Empty when unavailable or when every stored value is empty. A stored value named totp_secret is never listed or filled. Values are never returned. A totp entry is present when the credential has a TOTP seed; fill writes a generated code for it. Entries follow the connection's credential.

status.description: Items are created ready, which means the connection has a saved Kernel credential that stores values or a TOTP seed (what has_values or has_totp_secret report on credentials), not that a login succeeded. Unavailable means it no longer does; such items advertise no operations.

status_reason.description: Present when status is unavailable. connection_not_found means the connection was deleted. no_credential means the connection's credential was deleted or emptied after the item was created. external_credential means the connection was moved to an external credential provider.

It does not grant access until they approve in their app.

Present only for ready credentials with a customer-supplied access token, on single-item responses to callers that can use the vault. Each reference works only with that credential's access token and integration key.

status.description: revoking means the account was deleted or disconnected and Kernel is waiting for 1Password to confirm the revoke; it cannot be used and Kernel keeps retrying.

OnePasswordCredentialVaultItemSpecInput.description: A login request backed by a connected 1Password account or by a customer-supplied access token and matching integration key. Supply either account or both secrets, never both. Supplied secrets are write-only and never returned. Supply requests for new items; website remains supported for existing account-backed callers. To use an access request you already created and the user approved with the same access token and integration key, also supply access_request_id, resolved, and each requests entry's id; the item is created ready and Kernel doesn't create an access request.

access_request_id.description: ID of an approved access request you created with this access_token and integration_key. Requires resolved.

access_token.description: Customer-supplied 1Password broker token. Requires integration_key; stored encrypted on this item. Omit if providing a connected credential_account item via the account field.

access_token_expires_at.description: Optional supplied token expiry metadata for stored-token credentials. Omit if providing a connected credential_account item via the account field.

account.description: Key of a connected credential_account item in the same vault. Omit for stored-token credentials.

integration_key.description: Matching customer-supplied integration key. Requires access_token; stored encrypted on this item. Omit if providing a connected credential_account item via the account field.

resolved.description: Granted logins from 1Password's status for access_request_id, as returned by the 1Password SDK or extension. Requires access_request_id and an id on every requests entry. entryId may be omitted only when requests has one entry. Kernel doesn't verify the references; 1Password checks them when filling.

website.description: Legacy single-login shorthand. Supply requests instead.

access_request_id.description: Opaque request ID returned by the 1Password broker after a successful createAccessRequest call.

OnePasswordDisconnectVaultItemOperationR.description: End this account's 1Password connection and keep the item so it can be linked again. Fills stop at once. When no other vault uses the person's connection, Kernel revokes it at 1Password; if 1Password has not confirmed yet, this returns 409 provider_revocation_pending and Kernel keeps retrying. The account's credentials stop working until it is linked again.

OnePasswordFillVaultItemOperationRequest.description: Fill and submit an approved 1Password login in the selected browser page. The 1Password extension decides whether the approved login matches the page and refuses pages that don't. Supply entry_id when several entries are approved and the page origin does not identify exactly one of them, and target_id when more than one open page has page_url. The extension selects fields; callers cannot supply selectors or secret values. Submission does not confirm website authentication.

browser_id.description: Browser session ID, not a reusable browser name.

entry_id.description: ID of an approved request entry. Required when several entries are approved and the page's origin does not match exactly one of them.

page_url.description: Exact current top-level page URL. Must match exactly one open page in the browser unless target_id is supplied.

target_id.description: CDP target ID of the page to fill, such as tab.target_id from playwright.execute. Use it when several open pages have page_url. The page's current URL must equal page_url. Kernel brings the page to the front of its window before filling.

OnePasswordFillVaultItemOperationResult.description: The submission result reported by the 1Password extension when available. Kernel returns fill_unknown if the extension call has no conclusive result. Inspect the page to determine successful authentication on the website.

error_code.description: Present for fill_failed, and for fill_unknown when the extension reported autosubmitFailed (it filled and submitted the form but could not confirm the fill finished). These are allowlisted 1Password extension codes, never raw errors, secrets, or page content.

status.description: Kernel's outcome of the extension call. fill_submitted means the extension reported submission, not website authentication. fill_failed means the extension returned a known failure and includes error_code. fill_unknown means the form may have been filled or submitted without a conclusive result; inspect the page to see the result of the fill.

connect_url.description: 1Password connect link for the same authorization, for the person to open on their own device. In 1Password for iOS or Android it opens the app to approve the connection. Anywhere else it opens 1Password in the browser, where someone without 1Password can sign up; if the account is still pending afterwards, they connect with url. Also offer url to people who already use 1Password on a computer. Whichever link the person answers first settles the authorization and the other stops working. Expires with the account's expires_at; repeat the upsert for fresh links. Absent on a recovery link.

url.description: 1Password-hosted OAuth authorization URL for the human to open.

OnePasswordPollAccessVaultItemOperationR.description: Retrieve the status of a 1Password access request after presenting the approval link. Kernel paces checks on 1Password's schedule, timed from the first status check (at once, then every 2 seconds, slowing to every 10 and 20 seconds). Each call reads a fresh status, waiting up to 20 seconds for its first scheduled check. If 1Password rate limits the account, it returns 429 with Retry-After. After 3 minutes the approval prompt has closed; ask the owner whether they approved and check once more, or invoke 1pw_create_access_request for a new link. On a confirmed failed status, ask the end-user before deleting and recreating the credential item for at most one new request. Do not retry an uncertain dispatched request. The response contains no secret values. Credentials with a customer-supplied access token also return the granted references in state.access_request.resolved.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to keep checking on the schedule. The call still waits for its first scheduled check, at most 20 seconds, when that comes later.

OnePasswordRecoverVaultItemOperationRequ.description: Kernel encountered a recoverable error while linking this 1Password account. Use this action to get a new link to recover the connection. After recovery completes, start a new authorization on the same item.

OnePasswordRequestAccessVaultItemOperati.description: Request access to login entries in the end-user's own, non-shared 1Password vault. No browser is needed; the end-user approves access in the 1Password app. Shared-vault items and passkeys are not supported. Per-entry reason and keywords overrides are only supported for a single login entry.

reference.description: 1Password credential reference. Pass it unchanged as resourcePath to the extension's fillCredential or to the 1Password SDK.

OnePasswordUpdateAccessTokenVaultItemOpe.description: Replace only the access token on a stored-token 1Password credential. Preserves its integration key, request and approved references. Does not invoke 1Password or retry a pending/uncertain operation. For a wallet whose grant your backend refreshes, use update_access_token instead.

RegisterPasskeyVaultItemOperationRequest.description: Let a browser attached to the item's vault create a passkey on a website and store it in an empty passkey field. Only invoke when the item advertises `register_passkey`; declare the field first, for example by adding an optional passkey field with a credential update. Returns immediately; there is no time limit. The next passkey a page in that browser creates (`navigator.credentials.create`) is generated by Kernel, stored in the field, and only then returned to the page, so the website never receives a passkey Kernel failed to store. Each browser has one pending registration; a later `register_passkey` replaces it. Drive the website's "add a passkey" flow with your own browser tools, then confirm by reading the item (the field reports `has_value`) or its `credential_passkey_registered` event, and by signing in with `arm_passkey`. Only ES256 passkeys are created.

RemovePaymentMethodVaultItemOperationReq.description: Remove one payment method from a Kernel wallet, only when the wallet advertises remove_payment_method. Removal deletes the stored card and blocks new purchases, fills and confirmations funded by it without affecting the wallet's other payment methods; the wallet stays connected even with no payment methods left. A purchase funded by the method with an unresolved outcome blocks removal with 409 purchase_unresolved. If the provider outcome is uncertain the method stays in removal_pending and keeps refusing payments; retry the removal later. Removal is not proof that a payment did not occur. Scoped API keys require vaults:write in addition to vaults:use on this vault; otherwise the operation returns 403.
